body:
Should we mandate the use of the  ["Clear-Site-Data" HTTP response header](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Clear-Site-Data)?

[Browser support](https://caniuse.com/?search=clear-site-data) seems to be reasonable.

I can imagine that clearing all cookies on an origin might be undesirable but clearing the other items on logout seems more reasonable.

I would see this as a level 2 or 3 control.

What do people think?

comments.body:
Anyway I see it as just one possible technique to achieve:
* ~~V8.2.2 [MODIFIED] Verify that data stored in browser storage (such as localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, or cookies) does not contain sensitive data, with the exception of cookie-based session tokens in cookies and token-based session tokens in sessionStorage.~~
* V8.2.3 Verify that authenticated data is cleared from client storage, such as the browser DOM, after the client or session is terminated.

How separate requirement for the header could not be duplicate for those requirements?

Good question, IMHO this is less relevant for 8.2.2 but I guess this is a way of achieving 8.2.3. However, that now raises the question of whether it should be in chapter 8 or in the chapter with the other HTTP security headers (is that 14?) 

What do you think?

I see it as one technique to achieve V8.2.3 and I would not change it.

This `Clear-Site-Data` header is not webserver configuration (current V14.4) topic - you don't "hardcode" this header to webserver, but need to send it on logout situation from program code (correct?). It's similar to Set-Cookie header - you call it from program code when you need it, but not set it to web server configuration for every HTTP response.
So maybe we should add it as an example to the 8.2.3 requirement rather than requiring it explicitly?

It provides one technical solution, but I can see also negative part of (only) using this.

Let's say user was authenticated to some application and then lost internet connection - in this situation, client-side (browser) should be able to cleanup all the things itself.

So maybe we need to specify that as well:

> V8.2.3 Verify that authenticated data is cleared from client storage, such as the browser DOM, after the client or session is terminated. The "Clear-Site-Data header" may be able to help with this but the client-side should also be able to perform this clear up if the server connection is lost.
Ok, hard work, you got it in ;)
I do not think we should mandate it, 8.2.3 says "may" which I think is enough for now. Not browsers support this yet.
